title.en: 1. Three Major Geological Divisions of India
title.hi: 1. Three Major Geological Divisions of India

content.en:
Geologically, India is divided into three distinct regions with contrasting structures, rock types, and tectonic behaviors.

The Peninsular Block
  • Characteristics: The oldest, most rigid, and stable block of India. Primarily composed of ancient Archean gneisses and granites.
  • Stability: Has stood as a rigid shield since the Cambrian period, only experiencing minor vertical adjustments and coastal submergences.
The Extra-Peninsula (Himalayas)
  • Characteristics: Young, weak, and flexible geological structure. Formed by sedimentary deposits of the Tethys Sea squeezed between two colliding plates.
  • Tectonics: Active plate collision means the mountains are still rising, characterized by folding, faulting, and high seismicity.

3. The Indo-Gangetic Plains: A deep geological depression (foredeep) formed between the rising Himalayas and the stable Peninsula. It is filled with Pleistocene-to-Recent alluvial deposits brought by the Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra river systems. Its alluvium thickness ranges from 1,000 to 2,000 meters, making it the youngest geological region of India.

content.en:
The rock systems of India are categorized into four major eras, spanning from the oldest Precambrian base to recent sediments.

Archean and Purana Systems
  • Archean System: Gneisses and Schists forming the basement complex. **Dharwar System** is metamorphosed sedimentary rock containing India's major iron, manganese, copper, and gold deposits.
  • Cuddapah System: Famous for slates, quartzites, and limestone. **Vindhyan System** contains sandstone and diamond mines (Panna, Golconda).
Aryan Rock System (Coal & Volcanics)
  • Gondwana System: Formed in river basins; contains 98% of India's coal reserves. Highly fossiliferous (mainly plant fossils like Glossopteris).
  • Deccan Traps: Basaltic lava flows over 500,000 sq km, formed by fissure eruptions when India passed over the Reunion hotspot. Weathered into fertile **Regur (Black Cotton) soil**.

Comparison of Indian Rock Systems:

Rock System Geological Era Fossil Content Economic Importance & Minerals
Archean / Dharwar Precambrian (Archean) Unfossiliferous Metallic minerals (Iron, Manganese, Gold, Copper)
Cuddapah / Vindhyan Precambrian (Proterozoic) Unfossiliferous / Traces Limestone, sandstone, ornamental stone, diamonds
Gondwana System Carboniferous to Jurassic Highly Fossiliferous (Plants) Bituminous Coal (98% of India's reserves)
Deccan Traps Upper Cretaceous Rare / Intertrappean beds Building stone, bauxite, fertile Black Cotton Soil

Tectonic Cross-Section of Northern India:

Geological Section: Himalayas to Peninsula

Process & Chronology Flow
1
Himalayas (Folded)
2
Ganga Plain (Alluvium)
3
Peninsular Block (Stable Shield)
4
Himalayan Frontal Thrust (HFT)

title.en: 3. Physiographic Divisions Linked to Geological History
title.hi: 3. Physiographic Divisions Linked to Geological History

content.en:
The geological structure controls the physical features and soils of India, laying the foundation for its agricultural and economic zones.

Agricultural Plain Dynamics
  • Khadar and Bhangar: Newer (Khadar) and older (Bhangar) alluvial belts dictate crop suitability.
  • Karewas: Flat-topped terraces of lake deposits in Kashmir, highly valuable for saffron cultivation.
Industrial & Mineral Base
  • Chotanagpur Plateau: The mineral heart of India, composed of Dharwar and Gondwana structures.
  • Deccan Regur: Fertile black soil supporting the cotton textile hub of Western India.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is the oldest geological division of India?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Peninsular Block is a stable shield composed of ancient gneisses and granites, standing as the oldest geological block of India.

practiceQuestions.q: The Dharwar rock system is of immense economic importance because it contains:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Dharwar system is rich in metallic minerals like iron ore, manganese, copper, lead, zinc, and gold.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following describes the fossil content of the Archean rock system?
practiceQuestions.sol: Archean rocks formed before complex life existed on Earth, making them completely unfossiliferous.

practiceQuestions.q: What type of volcanic eruption formed the Deccan Traps during the late Cretaceous period?
opts: Quiet fissure eruptions of basaltic lava
Pyroclastic flow from a dome collapse
practiceQuestions.sol: The Deccan Traps were formed by quiet, non-explosive fissure eruptions as basaltic lava flowed over the landscape.

practiceQuestions.q: Which geological hotspot is linked to the volcanic eruptions that formed the Deccan Traps?
practiceQuestions.sol: As the Indian plate migrated northward, it passed over the Reunion Hotspot, triggering massive flood basalt eruptions.

practiceQuestions.q: The Indo-Gangetic-Brahmaputra plain is geologically classified as a:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Great Plains were formed by the filling of a foredeep (deep depression) created between the Himalayas and the Peninsula.

practiceQuestions.q: In which epoch of the Quaternary period did the major deposition of alluvium in the Northern Plains begin?
practiceQuestions.sol: The deposition of alluvium in the Indo-Gangetic foredeep occurred during the Pleistocene and Holocene epochs.

practiceQuestions.q: The Vindhyan rock system is highly famous for which of the following resources?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Vindhyan system yields building stones, limestone, and diamondiferous conglomerates (Panna and Golconda mines).

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following rock systems is the youngest in India's geological timeline?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Quaternary system (including recent alluvial plains and Karewas) is the youngest rock system of India.

practiceQuestions.q: The famous saffron-growing 'Karewa' terraces of the Kashmir Valley are geological deposits formed in:
practiceQuestions.sol: Karewas are flat-topped terraces composed of clay, sand, and silt deposited in ancient Pleistocene lakes.

practiceQuestions.q: Which tectonic event directly led to the upliftment of the Himalayas?
opts: The collision of the Indian Plate with the Eurasian Plate
The splitting of Gondwanaland from Laurasia
The volcanic eruption of the Reunion Hotspot
The sinking of the Indian Ocean floor
practiceQuestions.sol: The convergence and collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates squeezed the Tethys sediments, folding them into the Himalayas.

practiceQuestions.q: Which sea originally existed between the Indian Plate and the Eurasian Plate before the collision?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Tethys Sea lay between the northern Eurasian landmass and the southern Indian plate before its closure.

practiceQuestions.q: Why is the Himalayan mountain system described as geologically 'young and weak'?
opts: It consists of young, folded sedimentary rocks that are still tectonically active and rising.
It was formed by low-density dark matter.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Himalayas are young fold mountains composed of sedimentary rocks that remain flexible and seismically active.

practiceQuestions.q: Which mineral resource is Gondwana coal primarily classified as?
practiceQuestions.sol: Over 98% of Indian coal is of the Gondwana system, which is bituminous coal (medium to low grade, non-coking).

practiceQuestions.q: Which rock system contains the tertiary coal and lignite deposits found in Neyveli (Tamil Nadu) and Palana (Rajasthan)?
practiceQuestions.sol: Tertiary rock systems contain younger coal deposits, mostly lignite, found in Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, and Jammu & Kashmir.

practiceQuestions.q: The Chotanagpur Plateau, often called the 'Ruhr of India,' is mainly composed of rocks from which system?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Chotanagpur Plateau contains Archean gneisses, mineral-rich Dharwar rocks, and Gondwana coal basins.

practiceQuestions.q: Which geological system is bounded by the Narmada Rift Valley to its south?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Vindhyan range and its rock system lie directly north of the Narmada rift valley in central India.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the average thickness of the alluvial deposits in the Indo-Gangetic plains?
opts: It is only a thin layer of 5 meters
practiceQuestions.sol: The thickness of alluvial deposits in the Great Plains ranges generally between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.

practiceQuestions.q: Which soil type is formed by the weathering of the Deccan Trap basaltic rocks?
practiceQuestions.sol: The weathering of basaltic lava of the Deccan Traps yields fertile, moisture-retentive black soil (Regur).

practiceQuestions.q: In which geological division of India are landslides and earthquakes most frequent?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Himalayas are tectonically active and seismically unstable, making them highly prone to earthquakes and landslides.

practiceQuestions.q: The oldest fold mountains in India, now highly eroded as relict mountains, are the:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Aravalli Range is one of the oldest fold mountain systems in the world, dating back to the Archean-Proterozoic era.

practiceQuestions.q: The Cuddapah rock system is named after a district in which state where it was first studied?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Cuddapah system is named after the Cuddapah district of Andhra Pradesh, famous for quartzites, clay, and limestone.

practiceQuestions.q: Which rock system is known as the 'Basement Complex' of the Indian subcontinent?
practiceQuestions.sol: Archean gneisses and granites are the oldest crustal rocks, forming the basement complex upon which other systems were deposited.

practiceQuestions.q: The Gondwana rock system was deposited in which type of depositional environment?
opts: Continental river basins and lacustrine troughs
practiceQuestions.sol: Gondwana sediments were deposited in freshwater river basins and troughs (cratonic basins) during the Carboniferous-Jurassic eras.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is a primary characteristic of Gondwana coal?
opts: High moisture and high ash content, non-coking nature
practiceQuestions.sol: Indian Gondwana coal is mostly bituminous, containing relatively high ash content and requiring washing before industrial coking.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following mountain ranges is NOT a part of the Peninsular Block?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Pir Panjal Range is a part of the Lesser Himalayas, belonging to the Extra-Peninsular fold belt, not the Peninsular block.

practiceQuestions.q: The Tertiary system of rocks is of great economic importance in India because it holds:
practiceQuestions.sol: Tertiary sedimentary basins of Assam, Gujarat, and offshore Bombay High contain India's major petroleum reserves.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following geological systems is characterized by fossilized remains of the plant Glossopteris?
practiceQuestions.sol: Glossopteris is a fossil fern genus that is the index fossil for the Gondwana coal-bearing strata.

practiceQuestions.q: The term 'Traps' in Deccan Traps refers to which physical characteristic?
opts: Trapping of gas inside the lava
The step-like or stair-like topography formed by successive lava flows
Deep traps that hold underground water
A geological trap for volcanic dust
practiceQuestions.sol: 'Trap' is derived from the Swedish word 'trappa' (meaning steps), describing the step-like topography of basaltic flows.

practiceQuestions.q: The geological boundary separating the Ganga Plains from the Outer Himalayas (Shiwaliks) is the:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Himalayan Frontal Thrust (HFT) or Frontal Fault separates the alluvial plains of northern India from the Shiwalik foothills.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following represents the oldest rock formation in India?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Singhbhum Granite (part of the Archean craton) is one of the oldest dated rock blocks in India, dating back ~3.3 billion years.

practiceQuestions.q: In which geological era did the breaking up of Gondwanaland and the northward drift of the Indian plate occur?
practiceQuestions.sol: The fragmentation of Gondwanaland and the migration of the Indian plate began in the Mesozoic era (Triassic-Cretaceous).

practiceQuestions.q: Which rock system is known for providing the red sandstone used to build historical monuments like the Red Fort and Taj Mahal?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Vindhyan system is famous for yielding high-quality, durable red sandstone used in many historical Indian forts and palaces.

practiceQuestions.q: The marine fossiliferous deposits of Spiti Valley in the Himalayas belong to which geological era?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Spiti shales in the Extra-Peninsula are highly rich in marine fossils (like ammonites) from the Paleozoic and Mesozoic eras.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary reason why the Peninsular rivers like Godavari and Krishna flow from west to east?
opts: The Peninsular block tilts gently from west to east.
The earth's rotation pushes water east.
The western coast has high mountain ranges.
The rivers are blocked by the Aravallis.
practiceQuestions.sol: During the Tertiary era, the western margin of the Peninsular block tilted and subsided, leaving a gentle slope toward the East Coast.

practiceQuestions.q: The 'Bhangar' plains in northern India represent which geological deposit?
opts: Older, higher alluvial terrace above flood levels
practiceQuestions.sol: Bhangar is the older alluvium of the middle Pleistocene, forming upland terraces above the reach of regular river floods.

practiceQuestions.q: The 'Khadar' plains in northern India represent which geological deposit?
opts: Newer, low-lying alluvial deposits renewed by annual floods
practiceQuestions.sol: Khadar represents the newer, younger alluvium deposited in floodplains, which is highly fertile and renewed annually.

practiceQuestions.q: Which geological structure covers the largest area in the Peninsular Block?
practiceQuestions.sol: Archean gneisses and granites cover over two-thirds of the Peninsular block, forming the geological core.

practiceQuestions.q: The Deccan Traps lava flows occurred during which geological epoch?
practiceQuestions.sol: The fissure eruptions forming the Deccan Traps occurred between 68 and 60 million years ago, in the Late Cretaceous-Paleocene.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following minerals is NOT associated with the Dharwar rock system?
practiceQuestions.sol: Petroleum is found only in younger Tertiary sedimentary basins; Dharwar rocks contain metallic mineral ores.

practiceQuestions.q: The Vindhyan system rocks are largely unmetamorphosed sedimentary rocks. This indicates that:
opts: They have never experienced intense folding or tectonic deformation
practiceQuestions.sol: The Vindhyan basin remained tectonically stable after deposition, preserving horizontal layers of sedimentary sandstone and shales.

practiceQuestions.q: The Kolar Gold Fields (Karnataka) are associated with which geological rock system?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Dharwar schist belts of Karnataka contain the gold-bearing quartz veins of Kolar and Hutti.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following divisions of India is geologically considered a part of the ancient Gondwanaland?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Peninsular Block is a fragment of the ancient Gondwanaland shield that drifted northward to collide with Eurasia.

practiceQuestions.q: Which major fold mountain range in India was uplifted during the Tertiary period?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Himalayas were uplifted in three major phases during the Cenozoic/Tertiary period due to plate collision.

practiceQuestions.q: The sedimentary rock beds of the Shiwalik hills contain fossils of which fauna?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Shiwalik foothills (youngest Himalayan range) are rich in Tertiary mammalian fossils like elephants, rhinos, and ancestral pigs.

practiceQuestions.q: What name is given to the swampy, marshy geological tract lying north of the alluvial plains in northern India?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Terai is a swampy, damp zone created by emerging underground streams just south of the porous Bhabar gravel belt.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the 'Bhabar' belt?
opts: A narrow belt of gravel and boulders along the foot of the Shiwaliks where rivers disappear underground
practiceQuestions.sol: Bhabar is a porous belt of coarse gravel deposited by rivers exiting the mountains, causing small streams to flow underground.

practiceQuestions.q: The basaltic rocks of the Deccan Traps have a maximum thickness of over 2,000 meters in which region?
practiceQuestions.sol: The lava flows are thickest in the west (near Mumbai, up to 2,000m) and thin out toward the south and east.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following states contains the largest distribution of Vindhyan rock formations?
practiceQuestions.sol: Madhya Pradesh contains the largest exposures of Vindhyan rocks, forming the Vindhyan plateau and escarpments.

practiceQuestions.q: The geologic epoch that witnessed the birth of the Indo-Gangetic plains was the:
practiceQuestions.sol: The deposition of alluvium in the foredeep basin to form the Indo-Gangetic plains began during the Pleistocene epoch.

fact.en: Trap 1: Fossil Presence in Archean Rocks: Archean and Dharwar rock systems are completely unfossiliferous (contain no fossils) because they formed before complex life evolved on Earth. A common trap is matching Dharwar rocks with plant fossils.

fact.en: Trap 2: Coal type of India: Although coal is associated with Carboniferous systems worldwide, India's Carboniferous rocks are mostly marine and lack coal. 98% of Indian coal belongs to the younger Gondwana system (Permian-Jurassic), and it is mostly non-coking bituminous coal.

fact.en: Trap 3: Geological Stability: The Himalayas are not stable; they are young, weak, and flexible fold mountains still rising due to ongoing plate collision (seismically active Zone V). In contrast, the Peninsular Block is one of the most stable geological shields on Earth.

fact.en: Trap 4: Karewa Deposits: Karewas are lacustrine (lake-deposited) silt clays found specifically in the Kashmir valley. They are famous for **Saffron (Zafran) cultivation**, not tea or wheat.
